comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Follow-up on cc3e02e9:** reassessment of the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13096#issuecomment-5825961278) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13096#issuecomment-5833494722).

**Verified:** computing `leading`, `stepMonth` and `viewDate` at noon fixes the remaining cases. The `leading` finding and the pre-existing `viewDate`/`stepMonth` note are resolved, and the code comment is corrected. The original noon-cursor fix still holds (America/Santiago, September 2026 renders a continuous grid). No regressions were found in the clock panel.

```text
Africa/Cairo, August 2014, week start Sunday (Qt 6.11.2 V4)
          Sun  Mon  Tue  Wed  Thu  Fri  Sat   header        step from Jul / Sep
base    | (28) (29) (30) (31) (31)   1    2   JULY 2014     July / July
8127796 | (28) (29) (30) (31)   1    2    3   JULY 2014     July / July
cc3e02e | (27) (28) (29) (30) (31)   1    2   AUGUST 2014   August / August
```

Across all 341 tzdata 2026c zones, every month from 1800 to 2100 and all seven week starts, the head produced no wrong month step or header, and no wrong grid except grids containing a day skipped by a dateline change (for example `Pacific/Apia`, 2011-12-30), where base and the previous head also fail. Base and the previous head each had 2,008 wrong steps and 502 wrong headers, in the 502 zone-months whose local midnight on the 1st V4 moves onto the previous day. The latest of those is Cairo, August 2014. The only consumer of `viewDate` is the `Qt.formatDate` header, which uses only the date, so building it at noon changes nothing else.

| Earlier item | Status on cc3e02e9 |
|---|---|
| Noon cursor fixes the reported grid | Still holds |
| `leading` still uses local midnight | Resolved |
| `viewDate` and `stepMonth` at local midnight (pre-existing) | Resolved |
| Comment wording | Resolved in the code comment |
| Optional test improvement | Still open (optional) |

**Optional test improvement (unchanged):** the three new assertions, like the first, match source text. Each fails if its own line is reverted, but a behaviour-preserving rewrite also fails them, and adding `cursor.setHours(0)` after the cursor is built passes all 159 assertions while V4 repeats September 5 again under `TZ=America/Santiago`. Node cannot see the bug because V8 moves a skipped midnight forward. A behavioural guard needs UTC date arithmetic in `monthGrid` and `stepMonth`, or a small `qml6 -a core` check under `TZ=America/Santiago` and `TZ=Africa/Cairo` (August 2014 exercises `leading` and `stepMonth`).

**Related open PRs:** #10476 and #13186 build the same grid with `Date.UTC` instead, and #13127 makes the same four noon changes. The literal-source assertions here would not match either UTC implementation, and taking a UTC PR alone would leave `viewDate` (and, for #13186, `stepMonth`) at local midnight, so the code and tests of whichever approach is chosen need reconciling.

**PR description:** it still lists only the cursor change and still says V4 "rolls the date back a day" and that "noon exists in every timezone", which the corrected code comment does not say.

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up review of cc3e02e9 against the previous head 8127796 and base. Source review of the clock panel, Qt 6.11.2's V4 `Date` and `Qt.formatDate` conversion code, and the related open PRs' changes. Base, previous head and head ran in Qt 6.11.2's V4 engine through `qml6 -a core` (no window), comparing every grid cell, month step and header against UTC-computed values. The header check used the revision's exact `viewDate` expression in a standalone QML object rather than `Panel.qml`. The repository's clock test ran under Node on all three revisions and on labelled test mutants. No live Quickshell session was run. Results depend on tzdata 2026c and each zone's current standard offset.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
